root_idea.summary: The root primarily orients around stripping something of an outer covering—such as peel, leaves, or hair—leaving it bare or smooth.
root_idea.development: This orientation extends to leafless trees, barren land, beardlessness, smooth or polished construction, and figuratively to a person stripped of goodness and resistant to obedience. The food-softening branch is treated in the lexical evidence as related to the m-r-s root by substitution rather than as the central root development.

senses.definition: To become insolent, refractory, and rebellious; to turn away from obedience or good.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic context, the verb describes people who have become deeply resistant to obedience, with hypocrisy as the associated course of conduct.

senses.definition: To become habituated or inured to a condition, especially to persist in it.
senses.usage_conditions: With عَلَى and a following condition, as in مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفَاقِ, the construction is explained as becoming accustomed or hardened to hypocrisy; the same passage also carries the associated idea of persistence in that state.

senses.definition: Rebellious, insolent, and defiant of obedience; figuratively stripped of goodness.
senses.usage_conditions: An intensive epithet applied in the Quran to a devil, emphasizing resistance and rebellion rather than ordinary disobedience.

senses.definition: Rebellious, insolent, and resistant to obedience; bereft of goodness.
senses.usage_conditions: The adjective characterizes a being marked by persistent rebellion and departure from good; in the Quran it is used in descriptions of satanic or idolatrous opposition.
The Quranic use describes a constructed surface or structure as smooth and polished; the participle reflects the causative action of making something smooth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To soak, rub, mash, crumble, or otherwise soften food or another thing, especially in water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of bread, grain, or similar material softened by soaking and working it with the hand; the evidence also includes crumbling food into small pieces.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a thing smooth or polished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A surface-treatment use distinct from the food-softening usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a child, to mouth or suck the breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical evidence gives this as a specialized use of the verb with a nursing child as subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To keep eating softened dates prepared in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal use associated with dates soaked in milk until soft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become bare of leaves or herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a branch losing its leaves or of land becoming nearly destitute of vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a horse, to become without hair on the fetlock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a youth or young man, to remain without a beard or facial hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence concerns delayed or absent growth of the beard or cheek hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be bad, corrupt, or morally wicked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported synonymic explanation of the Form I verb, distinct from the more specific construction of becoming habituated to a condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push or propel a boat, or to drive something vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The nautical use involves propelling a vessel with a مُرْدِيّ; the evidence also records forceful driving more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strip a branch of its leaves or peel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causatively describes removing the outer covering from a branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A building made smooth and even, and described as tall or long or plastered with mud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the broader Classical constructional use of the passive participle; the Quranic occurrence specifically attests the smooth or polished aspect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Crumbled bread or similar food moistened with broth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective food noun for bread broken into small pieces and moistened; it is compared with ثَرِيدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fresh, juicy fruit of the arak tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun; the evidence distinguishes it from the ripe fruit named كَبَاثٌ in some accounts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pole or oar used to push or propel a boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nautical implement, synonymous with an oar in one cited explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural reported for this anatomical noun is مَرَارِيدُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A soft preparation of bread or dates soaked in water or milk and worked until flaccid; also water mixed with milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preparation may be mashed, rubbed, or pressed by hand after soaking; the evidence includes both food and the liquid mixture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or powerful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet is explicitly applied to evil beings of humanity or the jinn and to animals; in such uses it can carry an intensive force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lofty or high.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a building.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who often goes and comes because of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A characterization of active, lively movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leafless or barren: of a tree or branch without leaves, or of level sand or land where little or nothing grows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same adjective is extended from bare vegetation to a plantless expanse of sand or ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beardless youth or man, especially one without beard or cheek hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is applied to a male; the evidence distinguishes it from the feminine adjective used for a woman without pubic hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman without pubic hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feminine anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse without hair on the fetlock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equine adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mountain that presents obstacles to ascent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression جَبَلٌ مُتَمَرِّدٌ, describing a mountain that resists or obstructs the climber.

cautions: The Quranic construction مَرَدُوا عَلَى النِّفَاقِ supports both becoming habituated to hypocrisy and becoming refractory or turned away from good; these related but distinct interpretations are retained as separate senses.
The classical food-softening meanings are lexically recorded under this root, while the root-level etymological discussion treats them as related to مَرَسَ by substitution.
